page.layout: One printed page. Top: page number 15 centred above an ornamental rule. Then a centred heading INDEX CAPITUM. Below, a list of numbered chapter summaries in roman numerals, each with an italic entry, hanging left. Final catchword-like word CAP. at lower right.

main_text.head: INDEX CAPITUM.
main_text.l: I. Num aliunde potius regula humanarum actionum petenda sit, quam ex lege & euangelio?
II. An in Deo sint dua & quidem contraria voluntates?
III. An dua ista voluntates conciliari possint?
IV. An Deus velit peccata & ipsa per se decreverit?
V. An Deus efficaciter ordinarit, decreverit & voluerit, ut Adam laberetur?
VI. An omnia absoluta necessitate germantur?
VII. Quodnam sit primum Dei decretum?
VIII. Quaenam sit forma decretorum Dei?
IX. An credentes postquam semel verae fide donati sunt, possint peccatis suis gratia Dei & sua salute excidere?
X. Annon Bertius quemadmodum theologi, quorum sententiam arrodit, duplicem Dei voluntatem asserat?

page.notes: Ornamental rule above the heading is not transcribed. Several entries are set in italic with a decorative initial "E" or "Q" and a few words are hard to read in the scan (e.g. "germantur" in VI may be "germantur"/"geruntur"); the reading "necessitate geruntur" is the likely intended text but I have followed the visible letters as closely as possible. Final "CAP." is a printed closing mark, not a catchword.
